name: Analog Drive
description: Five circuits to push a sound through (tape preamp, console, transformer, triode, pentode), from weight and glue to a folded-over fuzz, with the level roughly held while you turn it up.

params.name: Drive
params.description: How hard the sound hits the circuit. The bottom of the travel adds weight and holds the peaks, the middle is clearly driven, and further up it compresses, thickens and finally squares off.

params.name: Circuit
params.description: What is being overdriven. Tape preamp is soft, warm and a little dull; Console pushes the mids forward with a firm edge; Transformer is thick in the low mids and breaks up the lows first; Triode is smooth and open and adds an octave-up glow; Pentode is lean and bright, stays clean and then bites.

params.name: Push
params.description: Sends the sound into the circuit far hotter, past anything Drive reaches alone, with the level brought back down after it. This is the setting that goes too far.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Takes the lows out before the circuit, so the bass stops driving it and the distortion gets tighter and thinner. At the bottom it is out of the path.

params.name: Thump
params.description: A resonant bump in the lows just above the Low Cut, going into the circuit, so that part of the sound is what breaks up.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Tilts the driven sound after the circuit. Down is darker and fuller, up is brighter and leaner.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: A steep filter after the circuit that takes the fizz off the top of the driven sound. At the top it is out of the path.

params.name: Auto Gain
params.description: On, the loudness stays about where it was while Drive changes the character; quiet sounds still come up a little as they are driven. Off, Drive also makes it louder, up to the circuit's ceiling.

params.name: Output
params.description: Level of the driven sound. The clean part of Mix is not affected. Very loud settings are held back softly before they reach the output.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the clean sound and the driven one. Part way keeps the clean attack and lays the grit under it.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Models five overdriven gain stages in outline (a tape machine's record amplifier, a discrete transistor console channel, an iron-cored class A stage, a triode and a pentode), not a circuit emulation of any unit. Each circuit is an emphasis filter into a static curve at a level-dependent working point and a de-emphasis filter out of it, so the circuits differ in tone and in which part of the spectrum saturates as well as in the curve; the transformer saturates on a low-shelved (flux-like) copy of the signal. The Drive knob is tapered so that the clean end stays clean and the middle is already well into the curve. The curve runs at four times the sample rate between linear-phase halfband filters, with second-order antiderivative anti-aliasing on top, after the approach of Parker, Zavalishin and Le Bivic, 'Reducing the aliasing of nonlinear waveshaping using continuous-time convolution', and of Bilbao, Esqueda, Parker and Valimaki, 'Antiderivative antialiasing for memoryless nonlinearities'. The low cut, Thump bell and high cut are trapezoidal state-variable filters, after the approach of Simper, 'Solving the continuous SVF equations using trapezoidal integration and equivalent currents'. Auto Gain is a static table per circuit measured on pink noise at -18 dBFS RMS, not a gain rider. The driven signal ends in a safety stage that is exactly linear up to 1.5 and lands softly on 4. All constants were set by measurement and judgement in this project, none taken from a source.
